quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

37 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel hard to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement slowly.
Brake hard and stop immediately.
Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, keep driving with the wheels off the pavement. Slow down gently by applying the brakes. When you are at a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to get back onto the pavement. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, what should you remember?

options.text: The road is extra slippery right when rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Leave more space when you need to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after rain starts. Your vehicle travels on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down when there is heavy rain, standing water, or slush on the road. This helps your wheels stay on the road.

questions.question: You are in the right lane on a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Check your side mirror for traffic and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal when you change lanes.

questions.question: Your accelerator gets stuck while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull the accelerator up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral right away and press the brake pedal firmly. When it is safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: When making a right turn on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal driving speed.
Stop and look for nearby police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: You may turn right on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. When turning, let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.
Traffic will increase ahead.
A steep hill is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the pavement is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, slow down. Do not brake or turn suddenly. Keep more distance between your vehicle and the car ahead.

questions.question: Another car is about to hit you. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Turn on your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.
No left turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and other vehicles?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other drivers.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leaving space between your vehicle and others gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must:

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights.
Use parking lights.
Use no lights.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop if:

options.text: You need to unload packages.
You need to avoid hitting another vehicle.
You need to let passengers out.
You stop for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You need to avoid hitting another vehicle.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can stop only to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: Your car takes longer to stop on:

options.text: Wet or icy roads.
Paved highways.
Roads at night.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on roads with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. You should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal to show them when it is safe to pass.
Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another driver passes you on the left. Look for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the other vehicle can move back to the right lane easily.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
A circular intersection is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
Lanes are reserved for buses and carpools.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for drivers with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: When you see this sign, it means:

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This chevron sign shows the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow. Multiple chevron signs may appear throughout the curve.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop.
Side road.
Two-way left turn.
Farm machinery.

questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs tell drivers to stop and yield at an intersection. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is green.
A traffic signal is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is at the next intersection.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in or entering a crosswalk. Stay alert for pedestrians at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Braking too much.
Braking suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.explanation: Your tires lose grip on water as you drive faster. At high speeds, they cannot clear water from the road, and your vehicle slides on a water film. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: What type of sign has this shape and color?

options.text: No passing zone
Wrong way
Railroad crossing
Stop

questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs are used only to mark no passing zones.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly. Grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas. When you are going very slowly, apply the brakes lightly and move to a safe area.

questions.question: What are regulatory signs?

options.text: They are placed everywhere there is danger.
They tell you what you must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn drivers about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. They show speed limits, no passing rules, no turning rules, and other driving laws.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
Flagger ahead.
Two-way left turn.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.explanation: This regulatory sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign tells you that the road ahead has low clearance.

questions.question: You stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track. What should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before going.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before going.
questions.explanation: Do not move as soon as a train passes. You must be able to see clearly down all tracks before crossing. Another train may be coming from another direction.

questions.question: When can you stop your car on railroad tracks?

options.text: If you are crossing and cannot fully clear the tracks.
If you do not hear any trains nearby.
Never.
If the gate is not down.

questions.explanation: Never stop on the tracks. If your car stalls, try to push it off. If you cannot, get help. Do not cross the tracks unless your car can completely clear them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop.
Fines double in a work zone.
Stop ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you that bicycles may cross the road.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your car before backing. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat.

questions.question: How can you avoid alcohol-related driving crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no to drinks if you are driving.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.explanation: Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices after drinking.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slower.
Pull over to the right and let other cars pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and let other cars pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road with traffic backing up behind you, you must pull over and let other vehicles pass. Only drive well under the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: A driver must go slowly through the intersection.
A driver must stop and then go when it is safe.
A driver must stop and then go when a green light or green arrow appears.
A driver may turn in the direction the red arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver must stop and then go when a green light or green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: Unless a sign says otherwise, a red arrow means drivers must come to a full stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.

questions.question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would interfere with other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you has broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with other traffic.
questions.explanation: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely and without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other cars are nearby.
Signal only if other cars are visible.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other cars are nearby.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Follow this law every time. Do not develop the habit of skipping it.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
An airbag can hurt an infant or small child, even in a low-speed crash.
Make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt before driving. Make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chances of being hurt or killed in a crash. Children age 12 and under should sit properly restrained in the back seat. Never place a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam.
On low beam.
Off. Use parking lights instead.
On either high or low beam.

questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when another vehicle is coming toward you or when you are following another vehicle at night. Use low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane only after you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
